$comment: The fixed 30-scheme reconciliation panel required by
docs/mf-analytics/06-QUALITY-COMPLIANCE.md §2. mfReconciliationJob loads THIS file at
runtime (it is a seed list, not test-only data — the path is the one 06 §2 names).
WHAT IS AND IS NOT IN HERE
Scheme code, scheme name and expected SEBI sub-category ONLY. There are deliberately no
expected return, TER or AUM values: those come from the external feed at run time, and a
checked-in 'expected' return would turn a reconciliation against an independent source
into a reconciliation against a number somebody typed in 2026 — which drifts by
construction and reports a breach every month for the rest of time.
⚠ THE SCHEME CODES ARE UNVERIFIED.
They were written from public knowledge of AMFI scheme codes, not from a live NAVAll.txt.
Every entry carries codeVerified: false and the job logs a warning naming them. SPOT-CHECK
EVERY CODE AGAINST A LIVE AMFI FILE BEFORE ENABLING THE JOB: a wrong code does not fail
loudly, it reconciles the right fund's numbers against the wrong fund's metrics and reports
a drift that no amount of debugging the metrics engine will explain. Verify a code, then
flip its codeVerified to true.
The panel is DIRECT-plan GROWTH options throughout, matching 03 §1's peer universes: an
IDCW option's published return is quoted on a NAV that steps down on every payout, so the
comparison would need the distribution history to mean anything.
Categories span equity (large/large-and-mid/mid/small/flexi/focused/value/ELSS), passive,
hybrid (aggressive/BAF/multi-asset/arbitrage/conservative), and debt (liquid/corporate
bond/gilt/short duration/banking-PSU/dynamic bond) so drift confined to one metric family —
a broken risk-free series, a bad TRI, an IDCW adjustment — shows up as a category pattern
rather than as scattered noise.
